headline: UNIDIR examined industry responsibility for military AI and marked Disarmament Week, as a hacker breached 100+ sites with an army of AI agents and Anthropic's leaked AI bill drew criticism as weaker than the FRONTIER Act.

points.text: UNIDIR examined industry responsibility in developing military AI, as the autonomous capabilities of weapon systems draw growing attention from the international community.
UNIDIR marked Disarmament Week with a piece on what makes people involved with armed groups put down their weapons, championing a people-centred approach to disarmament and reintegration.
SIPRI examined how to turn Women, Peace and Security commitments into action in defence budgeting.
ChinaTalk covered the Pentagon's $1 billion drone contest as part of a broader push for drone dominance.
A commentary argued Anthropic's leaked draft AI regulatory bill is weaker than the FRONTIER Act, undermining the company's 'safety first' pitch.
AI-generated deepfakes are producing reality-bending midterm election ads, as warnings about election disinformation come true.
A hacker breached more than 100 websites, including John Deere and SharkNinja, using an army of largely autonomous AI agents, according to security firm Norforge.
A judge ordered a former OpenAI engineer accused of spying on executives to remain in custody, likening the Saudi government's offer to secure his release to a 'blank check.'
